statement: In the pooled ridge model on demand lags 1-4 and 4/13-week rolling means (alpha=1.0, no log transform, no trend/category terms, no series-mean centering), adding the known-in-advance count of promotion weeks falling in the 4-week forecast window (treatment: promo=true) reduces relative WAPE of the next-4-week unit sum by at least 1.0% (SESOI) versus the identical model without that feature (comparator: promo=false), as estimated by the two-way (series x rolling-origin) bootstrap mean difference in relative WAPE under Design C (58 rolling origins, weeks 110-338, 364-week history).
kills_if: The two-way bootstrap 97.5% CI for the relative WAPE reduction (treatment vs comparator) includes 0 or its lower bound is below the 1.0% SESOI, or the point estimate is negative or null (e.g., promotion-week-count feature receives ~0 ridge weight across resamples), or the placebo control shows a non-null effect, or the positive control fails to show its expected effect — any of these drops the idea at alpha=0.025 per test.
rationale: This prereg describes only the frozen judge's actual treatment (known-in-advance promotion-week count in the forecast window) and its matched comparator, exactly per the locked machine config — not the last-year-same-4-week-window (YoY) feature the drafting request opened with; YoY targets a different mechanism (seasonal carryover vs. known promo calendar) and would need its own separate preregistration and judge run, since yoy=false in both arms here. Design is escalated from B to C per PI instruction: Design B's pilot data (pilot effect +1.96%, pilot SE 0.93%, alpha 0.025) gave only a 0.44 probability of a decisive result and 0.67 power at the 2.5% target effect — below the 80% power standard — so B is not lockable. Design C (58 rolling origins, weeks 110-338, 364-week history) is used instead to obtain enough independent origin-resamples for the two-way bootstrap to resolve the 2.5% target effect at 80% power against the 1.0% SESOI at alpha=0.025, despite its ~10x compute cost; Design A (6 origins) remains far too underpowered to consider. Leak canary is clean, and controls are specified per standard: positive control expected to show a supported effect, placebo control expected to show no effect — both are pre-registered checks on the same bootstrap pipeline, not separate hypotheses. No bias corrections or extra tuning are applied beyond the locked config (log=false, clip=null, window=null), consistent with the 'naive inverse transforms' constraint.
